Landscape 16:9 (1536x1024) scene for an animated explainer video. Precise drafting-table illustration on a mid-blue blueprint sheet (a clear medium blue, never dark navy or black) with a faint square grid, a thin white frame line inset from the edges and a small blank revision box in the lower-left corner. Every line is a steady white technical-pen stroke of one weight: straight edges ruled, curves drawn with a compass or French curve, no hatching, no shading, no gradients and no textured or filled areas, so water, glass, cloth and skin are all plain white outlines on the blue. A single sunflower-yellow highlighter tint appears ONLY inside Pip's glowing bulb, on arrowheads and on at most two key details; everything else stays white on blue. Lettering is tidy white capital drafting letters on a straight baseline, all in one style within a scene. Sizes and distances are shown with thin dimension lines that end in small arrowheads at both ends; weights, forces and temperatures are written as plain labels instead. People are minimal white stick figures: a circle head with two dot eyes, a short mouth line and a tuft of hair, a single-line torso, arms and legs, and plain stick hands; clothing is suggested at most by a collar tick or a hat brim, never drawn in detail, never coloured, and a person who returns in later scenes looks the same each time. Each hand belongs to an arm that joins a body, and two things held at once sit in two separate hands. Arrows, rays, waves, ground lines and furniture legs stop just short of any figure instead of crossing it; figures stand beside tables, not behind them. Arrows along one path all point the same way and run beside moving parts, never across ropes, belts or hinges. Light or sound reaching something is drawn as wavy lines ending in arrowheads at the receiver; rings spreading from a source mean it gives them off. Atoms are outlined circles joined by single straight bonds, exactly the atoms the scene names and the same drawing every time they return. Cut-away views show the inside behind a clean break line, never a ragged tear. An angle is marked by a small arc between the two lines it measures. If the scene poses a question, nothing in the drawing gives the answer away. Vehicles seen from the side face right unless the scene says otherwise. Boxes, panels, screens, cards, bars and badges are empty outlines, never solid fills. Gears mesh tooth into gap and neighbouring gears turn in opposite directions. Plants, flags and smoke lean the way any wind arrow points. Anything invisible to the eye, such as heat, radio or magnetism, appears only in a labelled diagram or on a screen, never on the real object. Cells, molecules, tools, icons and other diagram parts never get faces, arms or hands. Animals are plain white outlines with empty outlined markings. Size comparisons follow the numbers in the scene. Each label appears exactly once, and nothing overlaps the revision box. Scene: A paper boat drifts across a puddle beside a kerb, with two small ripples behind it. Use the attached sheet only as a reference for the pen style; the main character is NOT in this scene unless the scene text says so. No text, letters or words anywhere in the image. Keep the composition simple and readable, main subject centered with some empty paper around the edges. No logos, brand names or real people's likenesses. Everything is drawn the right way up and facing the way the scene describes (screens and pages face whoever is reading them). Stick-figure hands stay simple (Pip: small open circle hands); no extra or merged limbs.

The guide character (Pip) must match the attached character sheet exactly: a stick figure whose head is an old-fashioned round light bulb drawn in white outline, with a ribbed screw base for a neck and a coiled filament inside, the glass filled with a soft sunflower-yellow glow, two white dot eyes and a small curved white mouth on the glass. Below the screw base is a simple single-line body: exactly one torso line down to the hips, two arms that start on the torso a little below the base (never on the glass) and two legs, all single white lines, never outlined tubes or doubled strokes. Pip's hands stay at chest height or lower, pointing at or holding things, never lifted beside or above the bulb; a bent elbow or knee is still one line, and each hand is a small open circle as on the sheet (anything held touches the circle), never fingers, mittens or claws. Nib, when present, has a hexagonal pencil-stub head in white outline with a sharpened point on top, narrowed eyes, a small sideways frown and hands on hips, in white line only.
